subject: general
question: The marked price of an item is 25% more than its selling price. The selling price of the same item is 20% more than its cost price. The marked price of that item is what percentage more than its cost price?
solution:
**Given:-**

(1) The marked price of an item is 25% more than its selling price.

(2) The selling price of the same item is 20% more than its cost price.

**The formula used:-**** **

(1) Percentage more = [(MP - CP)/CP] × 100 

(Marked price with respect to the cost price)

Where, MP = Marked price 

CP = Cost price

**Calculation:- **

Let's assume the cost price of an item is 100y. 

The selling price of the same item is 20% more than its cost price. 

Selling price of the same item = 100y of (100 + 20)% 

⇒ 100y × 120% 

⇒ 120y (SP) 

The marked price of an item is 25% more than its selling price. 

Marked price of the same item = 120y of (100 + 25)%

 ⇒ (120y × 125) /100 

⇒ 150y (MP) 

⇒ Percentage more = [(MP - CP)/CP] × 100 

⇒ Percentage more = [(150y - 100y)/100y] × 100 

⇒ Percentage more = 50 %

** 

∴ The required answer is__ 50%__.**
